protocol.paired: same world states and range-sensor random stream per seed
protocol.paired_difference_interval: two-sided 95% t interval over seeds of (fused - range_only); descriptive seed-to-seed variation, not a generalisation claim

notes: Matching: one-to-one Hungarian assignment per timestamp with a 2.00 m Euclidean gate.
Evaluated tracks: confirmed and coasting snapshots only; tentative and deleted tracks are excluded.
Recall denominator: every ground-truth object in every simulated frame.
Precision denominator: every confirmed/coasting track snapshot in every frame.

Class accuracy: matched samples whose track class estimate and ground-truth class are both known (not UNKNOWN); correct / classified. None if no sample qualifies, so a range-only run never reports a fabricated zero.

Duplicate track sample: an evaluated track left unmatched in a frame while a ground-truth object lay within the 2.00 m matching gate (the object was claimed by another track). A duplicate track is a confirmed track that was never matched in any frame and has at least one duplicate sample.
Coverage: matched position errors against the reported 2x2 covariance; 95% threshold chi2(2,0.95)=5.991.

track_fragmentation: total interruptions, i.e. frames where a matched object goes unmatched and is matched again later, summed over objects (None if no object was ever matched). identity_switches counts track ID changes between consecutive matched frames and is independent of gaps.

scenario.description: Targets move at 2 m/s on distinct headings and cross at mid-run, adjacent targets 0.5 m apart at the crossing.
scenario.hypothesis: Near-coincident targets make association ambiguous: identity switches, unmatched confirmed tracks and fragmentation can rise even when the estimate of each target is accurate. Conclusions apply to a single crossing of a few targets under global-nearest-neighbour association.
scenario.name: crossing_targets

scenario.description: Heavy Poisson false alarms per frame: 4.0 on the range-bearing sensor (4x false_observations) and 8.0 on the vision sensor (about 2.7x false_observations).
scenario.hypothesis: Dense clutter creates many spurious candidates inside the gates; precision, unmatched confirmed tracks and lost-competition counts should worsen, and gate rejection is not a defence against clutter that falls inside the gate.
scenario.name: dense_clutter

scenario.description: Observations arrive 0.25+-0.05 s after capture (older than one epoch).
scenario.hypothesis: Observations older than the bounded one-epoch staleness policy are explicitly rejected and counted; no track can be maintained from them, so accuracy metrics are unavailable rather than silently computed from stale data.
scenario.name: out_of_sequence

scenario.description: Large vision bearing bias of 0.12 rad (well outside 1-DOF gate) while range-bearing is unbiased.

scenario.description: Moderate vision bearing bias of 0.015 rad (intended to pass the 1-DOF gate often) while range-bearing is unbiased.
scenario.hypothesis: A bias that passes the association gate will be fused and may degrade accuracy. This measures the trade-off between accepting more vision observations and introducing systematic error.
scenario.name: sensor_disagreement_within_gate

scenario.description: Moderate vision bearing bias of 0.020 rad (intended to pass the 1-DOF gate often) while range-bearing is unbiased.
scenario.hypothesis: A bias that passes the association gate will be fused and may degrade accuracy. This measures the trade-off between accepting more vision observations and introducing systematic error.
scenario.name: sensor_disagreement_within_gate_high

scenario.description: Moderate vision bearing bias of 0.010 rad (intended to pass the 1-DOF gate often) while range-bearing is unbiased.
scenario.hypothesis: A bias that passes the association gate will be fused and may degrade accuracy. This measures the trade-off between accepting more vision observations and introducing systematic error.
